notes.meaning: Zechariah sees Joshua the high priest standing in a heavenly courtroom before the Angel of the Lord. Joshua stood there not just for himself, but as a representative carrying the sins and failures of the whole Jewish nation. Satan, whose name means adversary or accuser, stood at Joshua's right side to bring charges against him.

The Lord Himself stops Satan's accusations by declaring that He has chosen Jerusalem and will not cast it away. Joshua is described as a charred stick snatched from a blazing fire, meaning God had already rescued him and the people from ruin in Babylon. Because God chose and rescued them by His own grace, Satan has no right to demand their destruction.

Joshua appeared before the angel dressed in stained, foul clothing. High priests were commanded to wear clean and beautiful garments, so these dirty clothes represent the shame and defilement of sin. Even though Joshua was covered in this filth, the Lord still graciously permitted him to stand in His presence.

The angel commands the attending angels to take off Joshua's dirty clothes. He explains that this action means He has forgiven Joshua's iniquity, which is his sin and guilt, and is dressing him in rich, clean robes. This picture shows that people cannot clean themselves from sin; only the Lord can remove our guilt and clothe us with His goodness.

Zechariah speaks up in the vision and asks that a clean turban be placed on Joshua's head. The turban was the special headpiece of the high priest, bearing the sign that he was holy to the Lord and fully restored to his sacred office. The angel of the Lord stood by, watching over the scene and giving His full approval.

The angel gives Joshua a solemn charge about his life and calling. If Joshua walks in God's ways and performs his priestly duties faithfully, he will rule over the temple and oversee its courts. God also promises him direct access to His heavenly court, granting him a place among the angels who stand before the Lord.

The Lord calls on Joshua and the other priests to listen, explaining that they serve as living signs pointing to the future. God announces that He is going to send His servant called the Branch, an Old Testament title for the coming Messiah. Like a fresh green shoot growing out of a cut tree trunk, this Savior would spring from David's royal family to bring new life.

God sets a stone before Joshua with seven eyes on it, picturing the Lord's perfect wisdom and constant, watchful care. The Lord promises to engrave this stone and wipe out the sin of the entire land in a single day. Christian readers see this fulfilled on the cross, where Jesus offered one complete sacrifice to take away human guilt forever.

The removal of sin leads directly to lasting peace and safety under God's blessing. Sitting under one's own vine and fig tree was an ancient Hebrew saying for enjoying rest, plenty, and freedom from danger. When people are at peace with God, they gladly invite their neighbors to enjoy that fellowship and security together.
